abi_findings: 107E0 has one real 32-bit frequency input; only its 1C1D8 callee reads an incoming argument.
10840 and 108E0 have six real o32 inputs: word, three bytes, halfword, word; setup takes the frequency address and can mutate it before initialization.

13D70 has two genuine unsigned halfwords, indexes a four-byte pointer table, performs a wrapping word decrement, reloads before two no-argument callbacks, and always forwards buffer/count and returns one.

The volatile flag is a supported source-level access hypothesis: native 202C4 explicitly sets and clears the same gate, and 1F13C reads it before continuing. It does not establish thread synchronization or prove the original declaration.
limitations: The two initializer wrappers remain nonmatches at 14/40 O2 despite complete behavior tests.
No hardware, asynchronous timing, external audio effects, native buffer bound, or cartridge integration proof is claimed.
